title: How a host discovers, reads and verifies an MCP skill
lede: The host model in this lab (the verifier) talks to a skills server. Nothing is read until a file is needed, every file is checked against the manifest, and approvals are bound to the set of files. Simulated: the server is in this app, nothing leaves the machine.

nodes.label: Host verifier
sub: approvals bound to the file set

nodes.label: Model context
sub: content tagged untrusted, with its origin

nodes.label: Approval store
sub: in memory, keyed by the resources set

steps.title: Connect
steps.what: The host asks which extensions the server declares. The skills extension and the resources capability must both be declared; if resources is missing, the host calls no skills method.
steps.why: A client must not call skills methods on a server that did not declare the extension.

steps.title: List: no file is read
steps.what: skills/list returns each skill's frontmatter and its manifest: every file's URI, size and SHA-256 digest. The listing may be partial.
steps.why: The retrieval counter on the Skills tab stays at 0.

steps.title: Get one skill by URI
steps.what: skills/get answers for any skill the server serves, even one the listing left out. Still no file is read.
steps.why: A partial listing is not proof that a skill does not exist.

steps.title: Read a file when it is needed
steps.what: resources/read fetches one file. The host checks the byte size and the digest against the manifest, and for SKILL.md compares the frontmatter field by field.
steps.why: A digest match is not a trust boundary: the digests come from the same server.

steps.title: Approve
steps.what: The person approves the skill, and separately scripts and allowed-tools. The approval is bound to the exact set of files.
steps.why: Approving scripts or allowed-tools never comes from the skill's own text.

steps.title: The manifest changes: approval revoked
steps.what: If a later skills/get lists different files or digests, the approval no longer matches and is dropped. Returning to the old manifest does not bring it back.
steps.why: Run the swap in the Approvals tab.

steps.title: Load into context, tagged untrusted
steps.what: Verified content enters the model context tagged with its origin server. This lab never executes anything; a real host would need a per-skill approval before it ran a script.
steps.why: Skill text is untrusted model input.
